Question B-007-008-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Tropospheric scatter is possible because tiny irregularities in the lower atmosphere redirect a small part of a VHF/UHF signal beyond the radio horizon.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Ionized patches in the troposphere": Ionized patches in the troposphere are not the mechanism; the troposphere is not an ionospheric layer.
- sourceIndex 2: "Increased daytime ionization of the D region": Increased daytime ionization of the D region affects lower HF absorption, not VHF/UHF tropospheric scatter.
- sourceIndex 3: "Local cloud cover": Local cloud cover by itself is not the cause; the important factors are small refractive-property variations.
